subject: Procurement: PO + Net terms request and invoice cadence
messages:
From: Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@novahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PO requirements, net60 request, and invoice batching question

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement reviewed the SOW and legal redlines. Two quick asks before we can issue a PO: 1) NovaHealth requires Net60 payment terms on all vendor contracts, and 2) we need the vendor to submit a single consolidated invoice monthly, rather than multiple invoices per project.

We can route the official PO to your AP once we confirm you can accept Net60 and monthly consolidated invoicing. If there's a standard amendment or an exception form you need signed, please point me to it.

Also attaching our PO template for reference (NovaHealth_PO_Template.docx).

Best,
Lisa Hammond
Sr. Procurement Manager
NovaHealth

--
Attachment: NovaHealth_PO_Template.docx (DOCX, 56KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@novahealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-15T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements, net60 request, and invoice batching question

Lisa —

Appreciate the clarity and the PO template. Quick answers up front: we typically operate on Net30, but we can consider Net45 or Net60 for enterprise contracts with a brief credit check and an approved finance exception. Consolidated monthly invoicing is fine — we can emit one invoice per month per account.

To move forward smoothly, two things from our side: 1) our finance team needs the final PO language to include the SOW reference and Redwood's billing contact; 2) for Net60 we usually require either an upfront partial payment (20%) or an invoice holdback clause while we enable the extended term — that’s an internal control, not a deal blocker.

Looping in Rishi (finance) and Marcus (legal) to confirm what form the approval takes and whether we can accept NovaHealth's exact PO template as-is.

Next steps: Rishi will confirm the credit/exception path; Marcus will review the PO template. If both are OK, I can approve going Carbon Copy to AP and we can expect the PO within 3–5 business days.

Thanks — talk soon.
Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@novahealth.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-16T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements, net60 request, and invoice batching question

Hi Lisa and Soojin —

Finance here. We can approve a Net60 term for NovaHealth provided we complete a standard credit review and add a clause for either: a 20% upfront retainer or an invoice holdback that preserves remedies if payment is delayed beyond 60 days. The holdback we typically use is a 10% retainage on the first two invoices.

Alternatively, if NovaHealth is comfortable with Net45 (no retainage), that's the quickest path. Net60 approvals usually take an extra 5–7 business days because of the extended exposure.

Soojin, I can sign off on an exception once Procurement confirms the preferred path (retainer vs. holdback) and we get the completed credit form.

Rishi
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: marcus.lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@novahealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements, net60 request, and invoice batching question

Lisa —

Thanks for the template. Quick legal notes: we need the PO to reference the countersigned SOW (Signed_SOW_NovaHealth_v3.pdf) by filename and date; we cannot accept unilateral modification clauses, and we prefer payments to be made to Redwood Inference, Inc. with our W-9 included. If your template has an indemnity or audit clause that looks broad, we may need to carve out typical SaaS limitations — happy to mark up and return.

If Procurement can accept a one‑page amendment that lists: net terms, invoice cadence, remittance details, and SOW reference, it speeds execution. I’ve attached the signed SOW for reference.

Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Signed_SOW_NovaHealth_v3.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@novahealth.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: 2026-06-17T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements, net60 request, and invoice batching question

Marcus / Soojin —

Thanks, all. Procurement prefers to avoid upfront retainers — they asked us to confirm if Redwood can accept a 10% retainage on the first invoice only as a compromise. They can stretch to Net60 if the retainage language is present. If Redwood can accept Net45 with no retainage, they would prefer that for faster processing.

I'll attach a proposed PO once I have confirmation on those two options. Either way, NovaHealth will include the SOW filename in the PO.

Lisa

--
Attachment: (none)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@novahealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements, net60 request, and invoice batching question

Lisa —

Thanks for the update and for being flexible. Redwood can proceed with either: (A) Net45 with no retainage (preferred, faster), or (B) Net60 with a 10% retainage on the first invoice only. If you want the fastest execution, confirm Net45 and we will accept the PO and start onboarding immediately.

If NovaHealth confirms Net60 + 10% retainage, note that our finance team will run the credit/exception and expect a 5–7 business day approval window.

Please send the PO PDF when ready and we’ll countersign.

—
Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
